entities.name: Seville Cathedral
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Cathedral of Saint Mary of the See in Seville (Catedral de Santa María de la Sede), built between 1401 and 1506 on the site of the Almohad Great Mosque of Seville, is the world's largest Gothic cathedral by floor area, the third-largest church by volume, and the burial site of Christopher Columbus — making it simultaneously the greatest achievement of Gothic ecclesiastical architecture and a monument to the Age of Exploration's most consequential figure. The Giralda bell tower (originally the Almohad mosque's minaret, 1184-1196) was incorporated into the cathedral as a symbol of Reconquista triumph.

When the Almohad mosque was converted after the Christian reconquest of Seville (1248), it served the Christian community until the 15th century chapter decided to build 'a church so beautiful and so great that those who see it finished shall think we were mad.' The 116-year construction produced the largest Gothic building in the world by floor area (11,520 m²), with 80 chapels, 93 stained glass windows, and the Capilla Mayor altarpiece (the world's largest retable, 20.5 × 18 meters, with 36 scenes in gilded wood).

Columbus's remains were transferred to Seville from Havana in 1898 after Cuba's independence from Spain, and his coffin is carried by four figures representing the kingdoms of Castile, León, Aragón, and Navarre. The Giralda tower — the Almohad minaret completed in 1198 with a ramp system (not stairs) allowing mounted horses to ascend for the call to prayer — was topped with Renaissance additions in 1568, becoming the model for hundreds of cathedral towers in the Americas built by Spanish colonial church builders.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Seville Cathedral — the world's largest Gothic church and Columbus's tomb — synthesizes the two defining events of Spanish medieval history: the Reconquista's defeat of the Almohad Caliphate (the Giralda minaret converted to bell tower) and the discovery of the Americas (Columbus's remains).
